items.title: Building a safer path to autonomous industrial AI
items.raw_text: Industrial AI is entering a new phase. After decades of predictive analytics and other specialized applications, advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI are making it possible to automate more complex tasks across industrial environments. But unlike AI that operates purely in the digital world, industrial AI can interact directly with physical systems, where an unexpected decision can have consequences for safety, reliability, and critical infrastructure. That makes responsible deployment central to the next wave of industrial automation. “How do we leverage these technologies while maintaining safety, while maintaining reliable operations, while still being able to deliver on the promises of the new capabilities?” asks Arti Garg, chief technologist at AVEVA. The challenge is particularly acute as newer AI systems become more capable but also harder to predict and explain. One foundation for making that transition work is data. Industrial systems often contain information across telemetry, service logs, engineering documents, and other disparate sources. Newer technologies can help connect and correlate that information more quickly, giving operators real-time support when diagnosing problems. AI-powered robots could take that a step further by gathering information in hazardous environments without requiring workers to enter them. items.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging
items.raw_text: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging Some excellent writing advice from Michael Lynch. Michael warns against "meandering intros", misjudging your reader's existing knowledge, assuming they'll read your previous posts, and excessive formality. He also warns against overreliance on links as an excuse not to explain terminology. This one hurt! I do this all the time, but I have a nagging suspicion that almost nobody ever clicks on them. (In a Lobste.rs comment Michael clarifies that "My rule of thumb is that my article should still make sense to the reader even if they don't click any links". That works for me.) This point about using your own voice is crucial: Beginner software bloggers suffer from a mass delusion that you have to write in a stiff, overly formal way for people to take you seriously [...] Just write the way you talk. With so many developers delegating their writing to AI, software blogging is becoming bland and homogenous. Readers are hungry for writing with personality. items.title: Probiblio zoekt lid Raad van Toezicht met financiële kennis
items.raw_text: Draag jij bij aan de toekomst van bibliotheken in Noord- en Zuid-Holland? De RvT is op zoek naar een generalist die beschikt over duidelijke affiniteit met financiën en bij voorkeur kennis heeft van de bibliotheekwereld. Het lid krijgt zitting in de audit-commissie naast een ervaren collega-lid. Gezocht wordt een beginnend RvT lid dat open en transparant acteert en in staat is zelfreflectie toe te passen. Probiblio ondersteunt en adviseert bibliotheken in Noord- en Zuid-Holland om ze sterker te maken voor de toekomst. De branche werkt met een Bibliotheekconvenant waarin de gezamenlijke afspraken staan voor de jaren 2024 – 2027. De focus ligt in deze periode op de geletterde samenleving, participatie in de informatiesamenleving en een leven lang ontwikkelen. We zetten ons in voor een bibliotheekbranche die meebeweegt met de samenleving en waarin iedereen toegang heeft tot kennis en cultuur. De rol van de Raad van Toezicht De RvT van Probiblio werkt volgens de statuten van Probiblio en de Governance Code Cultuur . De raad vervult drie rollen: toezichthouder, sparringpartner van de bestuurder en werkgever van de bestuurder. De leden van de RvT houden actief, kritisch en op stimulerende wijze toezicht. Zij bewaken de maatschappelijke doelstelling en de continuïteit van de organisatie. Kijk hier voor meer informatie: Uitgangspunten van de Raad van Toezicht van Probiblio . items.title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones
items.raw_text: For a while, those hoping to avoid the difficulty and expense of dealing with Adobe's Creative Suite have been able to use several free and/or open-source alternatives that replicate some or all of those capabilities. Now, one developer is using AI-powered reverse engineering to mimic the look, feel, and functionality of Adobe's well-known software with what he hopes will soon be perfect fidelity. Artcraft got its start last year as a "controllable AI for artists" that allows for precise post-generation editing of AI-crafted images and videos. Over the weekend, though, the brand debuted its pivot to a suite of seven open source apps recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe's Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. In announcing those new apps on Reddit earlier this week, software developer Brandon Thomas said he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to create "clean-room replacements" for Adobe's closed source software in Rust (with WebAssembly versions available for use in a browser). And while commenters on Hacker News and elsewhere have taken pains to point out the new software's many current shortcomings, Thomas make the grandiose promise that the current "super early alpha" state will soon lead to something just as functional as anything Adobe has ever put out. items.title: PA measles outbreak tops 1,000 cases, largest since disease was eliminated
items.raw_text: Pennsylvania's explosive measles outbreak is now the largest the US has seen since the highly infectious virus was declared eliminated in 2000. With well over 1,000 cases, it's the largest on record since 1991. Pennsylvania's health officials reported 1,078 measles cases in all of 2026 as of this afternoon. That includes 12 cases in January and March, with the remaining 1,066 cases since April , when the current outbreak began. The tally includes 145 cases recorded in the last seven days and 74 identified since the previous update on Monday. Health officials noted that 40 of the 74 cases added today were from more than two weeks ago and are just now being recorded. Among the cases, there have been 207 hospitalizations and five deaths— a newborn , a 6-week-old , an 18-year-old , a 20-year-old , and a 40-year-old . All of the deaths occurred during the current outbreak in people who were unvaccinated; the two infants were too young to have been vaccinated. Read full article Comments

Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
items.raw_text: Life is remarkably selective. Life relies on many molecules with what is termed "handedness"—they're chemically identical but are mirror images of each other. Most chemical reactions will make a 50-50 mix of the left- and right-handed forms of a chemical, but life uses only one of them. In fact, because of the differences between left- and right-handed chemicals, most of the key enzymes used by organisms will fail to work if they're presented with chemicals that have the wrong handedness. That poses a bit of a challenge for origin-of-life research, as we're forced to explain how a world that may have started with an even mix of left- and right-handed chemicals produced organisms that only used one of them. Today's Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to two individuals, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai, who discovered chemical reactions could be biased, producing large excesses of one of the two forms of a chemical. items.raw_text: Hi HN! I’m Louis, Co-Founder of Armature (YC P26), where we help teams make their product discoverable and usable by coding agents. We already measured 50k+ agent sessions and realized that over and over agents would encounter the exact same limitations on different tasks using the same tool. So we wondered why these weren’t fixed. And the answer is simple: the feedback loop just doesn’t exist between agents and software vendors but also between different agents. Humans can share their experience on platforms like https://g2.com and https://trustpilot.com , but agents have nowhere to. So we created: https://agent.reviews : the G2 for agents. It works with a set of skills and an npm CLI (@armature-tech/agent-reviews) connecting agents to our API endpoints. Anyone can ask their agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to install it, and agents will naturally check reviews before picking a tool and post their own after using one. The new 1 trillion-parameter model, Mistral Large 4—nicknamed Le Chonk—can be used and customized by anyone. It’s currently available in preview, with a final version to follow by the end of the month. Though Le Chonk is built to compete with leading general-purpose models, it’s optimized specifically for coding and cyberdefense, as well as tasks particular to manufacturing, finance, electrical engineering, and other niches. “There are a lot of areas where the other labs will not focus that much,” Guillaume Lample, cofounder and chief scientist at Mistral, tells WIRED. “There are so many domains in which you can improve models.” Read full article Comments

items.title: AI-assisted proof of optimal packing for 11 squares
Google rolls out improved SynthID AI content detector, now available globally
items.raw_text: Every piece of AI content from Google's Gemini models has a hidden SynthID label, which makes it very difficult to pass the content off as authentic . SynthID has also gotten buy-in from other major AI players, but actually checking for those invisible watermarks has been a convoluted process. It's going to be a little easier going forward, though. Google has announced that its SynthID detector now supports watermarks from all its partners, and it's available for anyone to use on a new dedicated website. SynthID is an invisible signal encoded in the pixels of AI-generated images and videos, and in the waveform of AI audio. Google says Gemini alone has integrated SynthID with over 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio. Until now, the only way for those outside of Google's trusted tester program to check for SynthID was to ask Gemini. This is rather clunky, and the model's output could sometimes be confusing when you just wanted a simple "yes" or "no." Now you can cut Gemini out of the loop. Starting today, you can go to the new SynthID.com website to check a piece of content for an AI watermark. A major limitation of Google's previous detector was that it only checked for Google's version of SynthID. Even though ChatGPT images, for example, have SynthID, they wouldn't be flagged in Google's detector. That's no longer a problem. Read full article Comments

items.title: AI/ML is becoming a performance factor in motorsport
items.raw_text: There’s been something of a change in the world of motorsport over the past few years. It has to do with where the money comes from. In the old days, it was tobacco and, to a lesser extent, booze. Today such things are mostly banned, and when you look at a racecar covered in sponsor logos, you’re likely to see something crypto-, cyber-, or AI-related. This makes sense—an ever-larger share of our GDP is wrapped up in those segments. They’re the ones with all the money, and it takes money to go racing. So at the amateur level, we’ve seen tech CEOs replace dentists as the privateer of choice: This past weekend’s Petit Le Mans included co-founders of GitHub, CrowdStrike, Shopify, and the creator of Ruby on Rails, to name a few. But this is an instance where a sponsor can provide tangible benefits to their motorsports partner beyond a bank transfer, as Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) and OpenAI have been showing in IndyCar this year. items.raw_text: Thuiswinkel.org start vandaag met Thuiswinkel Scam Protectie, een dienst die continu zoekt naar nepwebshops en valse domeinnamen die bestaande merken nabootsen. Als een van de aangesloten leden slachtoffer wordt van namaak, kan de site na constatering offline worden gehaald. De branchevereniging doet dat niet zelf. De dienst is ontwikkeld door en wordt uitgevoerd door Brandsolo . Brandsolo uit Amsterdam monitort het web doorlopend op scamshops en misleidende merkdomeinnamen. Het bedrijf gebruikt zo’n 75 variabelen om te toetsen of een site echt of nep is. Te denken valt aan zaken als de KvK-gegevens, url’s en logo’s. Wordt een nepsite aangetroffen, dan krijgt het betreffende Thuiswinkel-lid via een portal een melding. Brandsolo kan vervolgens de site offline laten halen. De monitoring is gratis. Verwijdering kost geld. De timing berust niet op toeval. Richting Black Friday en de feestdagen zoeken consumenten volop naar aanbiedingen, populaire en vooral goedkope producten. items.raw_text: De top 1 procent abonnees bij AI’s neemt bijna een vijfde van alle consumentenuitgaven voor zijn rekening, meer dan de onderste helft van alle betalers samen. Dat blijkt uit de zevende editie van de Top 100 Gen AI Consumer Apps van investeerder Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Voor het eerst baseert de ranglijst zich ook op bestedingsdata, aangeleverd door onderzoeksbureau YipitData. De cijfers bevestigen wat velen al weten, dat AI wijd verbreid wordt ingezet. Bijna de helft van de Amerikaanse consumenten zegt AI te gebruiken, maar slechts 25 procent doet dat dagelijks. In augustus had 4,5 procent een betaald persoonlijk abonnement op ChatGPT, Gemini of Claude, tegen 2,1 procent een jaar eerder. Het aantal betalers is dus ruim verdubbeld, maar het blijft een bescheiden groep. Binnen die kleine groep is de verdeling scheef. De top 10 procent abonnees is goed voor ongeveer de helft van alle waargenomen uitgaven. De top 1 procent betaalt gemiddeld 903 dollar per maand en neemt 19,5 procent van de uitgaven voor zijn rekening, tegen 16,6 procent voor de onderste vijftig procent samen. Daar komt bij dat deze groep powerusers ook grif de portemonnee trekt voor andere AI-tools voor meer specialistisch werk. Te denken valt aan n8n, fal, Manus, Hermes Agent, Higgsfield, Figma en HeyGen. Het rapport zegt weinig over advertising omdat dat nog een kleine markt is.
